questions.text:
In a system, there are three types of resources: E, F and G. Four processes [latex]P_0,P_1,P_2 \; and \; P_3[/latex] execute concurrently. At the outset, the processes have declared their maximum resource requirements using a matrix named Max as given below. For example, Max[[latex]P_2[/latex],F] is the maximum number of instances of F that [latex]P_2[/latex] would require. The number of instances of the resources allocated to the various processes at any given state is given by a matrix named Allocation.
Consider a state of the system with the Allocation matrix as shown below, and in which 3 instances of E and 3 instances of F are the only resources available.

From the perspective of deadlock avoidance, which one of the following is true?
questions.solution:
Need = Max [latex]-[/latex] Allocation: P0 (3,3,0), P1 (1,0,2), P2 (0,3,0), P3 (3,4,1). Available (3,3,0).
- P0 can finish [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] available (4,3,1)
- P2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (5,3,4)
- P1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (6,4,6)
- P3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] (8,4,6)

Safe sequence P0, P2, P1, P3 exists.

Answer: The system is in safe state

options: The system is in safe state.
The system is not in safe state, but would be safe if one more instance of E were available
The system is not in safe state, but would be safe if one more instance of F were available
The system is not in safe state, but would be safe if one more instance of G were available

questions.text: Consider a system with 3 processes that share 4 instances of the same resource type. Each process can request a maximum of K instances. Resource instances can be requested and released only one at a time. The largest value of K that will always avoid deadlock is ____.
questions.solution:
Deadlock is impossible if, even when every process holds K [latex]-[/latex] 1 instances, one instance is still free: [latex]3(K-1)+1\le4\Rightarrow K\le2[/latex].

With K = 3, two processes could hold 2 each and wait forever.

Answer: 2

questions.text:
Consider a process executing on an operating system that uses demand paging. The average time for a memory access in the system is M units if the corresponding memory page is available in memory, and D units if the memory access causes a page fault. It has been experimentally measured that the average time taken for a memory access in the process is X units.
Which one of the following is the correct expression for the page fault rate experienced by the process?
questions.solution:
With page fault rate p: [latex]X=(1-p)M+pD=M+p(D-M)[/latex].

[latex]p=\frac{X-M}{D-M}[/latex]

Answer: (X - M) / (D - M)

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text: Which of the following statement is true?
questions.solution:
Jitter is the variation in timing. A hard real-time OS must meet every deadline exactly, so it has less jitter than a soft real-time OS.

Answer: Hard real time OS has less jitter than soft real time OS

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Hard real time OS has less jitter than soft real time OS
Hard real time OS has more jitter than soft real time OS
Hard real time OS has equal jitter as soft real time OS

questions.text:
The Linux command
 mknod myfifo b 4 16
questions.solution:
mknod name b major minor creates a block special file (device 4,16); 'c' would make a character device and 'p' a FIFO. Creating device files requires root.

Answer: will create a block device if user is root
